rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Humans (Homo sapiens) are primates in the family Hominidae. Evolution proceeded from bipedal Australopithecus through tool-using Homo habilis and fire-using Homo erectus to Neanderthals and modern Homo sapiens. Key adaptations include bipedalism, brain enlargement, loss of body hair, and the development of language and culture.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Taxonomic position: Animalia > Chordata > Mammalia > Primates > Hominidae > Homo > Homo sapiens
Evolutionary sequence: Australopithecus → H. habilis → H. erectus → H. neanderthalensis → H. sapiens
Key adaptations: bipedalism, encephalisation, language, culture

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Humans are NOT apes; we are hominids (great apes) within the family Hominidae, but a distinct lineage.  ·  Australopithecus was bipedal but had a small brain (~400–500 mL); the brain enlarged later in Homo.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Position of humans: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, Species Homo sapiens.  ·  Primates: grasping hands, forward-facing eyes, large brain; include prosimii (lemurs), monkeys, apes, and humans.  ·  New World vs Old World monkeys: New World (Platyrrhini — flat nose, New World); Old World (Cercopithecinae — narrow nose, Old World).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Apes (no tail): gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan, gibbon, humans (hominids).  ·  Human evolution: bipedalism → tool use → fire → brain enlargement → language.  ·  Fossil evidence: Lucy (Australopithecus), Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Neanderthals.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Molecular: ~98.8% DNA similarity with chimpanzees; divergence ~6–7 Ma.  ·  Homo habilis (the "handy man") made stone tools; Homo erectus (the "upright man") controlled fire and left Africa.  ·  Neanderthals were NOT primitive; they made tools, buried dead, and had larger brains on average than modern humans.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Bipedalism (upright walking) evolved BEFORE the large brain — a key sequence in human evolution.  ·  Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor (~6–7 Ma); we did not evolve "from" chimpanzees.  ·  Homo neanderthalensis — robust, large brain, cold-adapted, extinct ~40,000 years ago.
